text_blocks.snippet: While COVID-19 and the common cold share some symptoms, there are key differences to help distinguish them. COVID-19 symptoms typically appear 2-14 days after exposure and may include fever, cough, fatigue, and a new loss of taste or smell, sometimes with shortness of breath. Cold symptoms appear 1-3 days after exposure and usually involve a runny or stuffy nose, sneezing, sore throat, and potentially a mild fever.
